BiblicalUsage: Addiyr is a word for size and majesty — the mighty waters of the Red Sea, the Lord's excellent name, the nobles and princes of the nations. It describes whatever stands tall and commands notice, from a great cedar to a king. Most often it is used of God Himself, whose name and whose power are excellent above all.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that addiyr matters because it gives us a word for God's sheer scale. He is not merely better than the idols or the kings — He is majestic in a way that makes everything else look small, and His name carries that weight wherever it is praised.
